stories.headline: Manila Raises $1.26 Billion From Retail Dollar Bonds at 5.65%, as Slate Grocery Holders Back a $2.3 Billion Buyout
stories.summary: The Philippine Treasury said on 26 Nov it raised $1.26 billion, about P80.4 billion, from its third retail dollar bond, more than double its $500 million minimum target: $453.4 million came from the 19 Nov auction and $806.09 million from the public offer that ran to 24 Nov. The three-year notes pay 5.65% and mature on 27 Nov 2029. In Canada, Slate Grocery REIT unitholders approved its sale to Brixmor Property Group and Everview Partners for US$13 a unit in cash, valuing the trust at US$2.3 billion, with 98.9% of votes in favour (reported 26 Nov). India's NSE won RBI and SEBI no-objection letters to launch futures on corporate bond indices (26 Nov).
stories.market: The Manila deal matched the 2023 retail dollar issue and taps local dollar savings at a time of high global yields; the Slate vote leaves only an Ontario court order and an Investment Canada Act review before closing.

body: The Philippines' third retail dollar bond (RDB 3) raised $1.26 billion, equal to the October 2023 offering and below the $1.6 billion of the 2021 debut. National Treasurer Sharon Almanza had set a minimum of $500 million. The proceeds will fund the budget's priority programmes.

Slate Grocery REIT, which owns US grocery-anchored shopping centres, won 98.9% approval for its cash sale to Brixmor and Everview Partners at US$13 a unit, a deal first announced in September. Closing still needs a final Ontario Superior Court order and Investment Canada Act clearance.

In India, NSE received no-objection certificates from the RBI and SEBI to introduce futures contracts on corporate bond indices, with trading details to follow. Titan Company separately repaid Rs 1,075 crore of commercial paper at maturity.

stories.headline: Halfords Soars 15.6% on a 66% Profit Jump and Raised Floor, Tullow Gains 7% on Output, While Bachem Sinks 12% on New Targets
stories.summary: Halfords said first-half underlying pre-tax profit rose 66% to £39 million on 7.1% like-for-like sales growth and lifted the bottom of its full-year profit range to £60-65 million from £55-65 million; the shares jumped 15.6% to top the FTSE 250 (26 Nov). Tullow Oil said 2026 output will beat the top of its 34-42 kboepd range after averaging about 45.2 kboepd to October, and rose about 7%, though it cut free-cash-flow guidance to $160-210 million after a $112 million Ghana tax payment. Swiss drug-ingredient maker Bachem fell as much as 12% after setting 15-18% annual sales growth and 33-35% EBITDA margin goals to 2031 alongside heavy capex. Poland's Text Group rose about 17% on a quarterly profit beat (26 Nov).
stories.market: The FTSE 100 rose 1.8% to 10,609.3 and the FTSE 250 1.9% on 26 Nov, with company news behind the biggest single-stock moves in both indexes.

sources.name: Tullow Oil RNS via TradingView, 26 Nov

body: Halfords' underlying pre-tax profit for the half to 2 Oct rose 66% to £39 million and statutory profit more than doubled to £35.5 million from £17.2 million. About £8 million of the gain came from the hot summer; excluding weather, profit rose about 32%. The retailer warned it does not expect first-half like-for-like growth and margins to be repeated in the second half and said it may have to pass on further price rises if Middle East-related costs climb.

Tullow's trading update put group production at about 45.2 kboepd in the ten months to end-October, including 7.5 kboepd of gas, so full-year output will exceed the top of its 34-42 kboepd guidance. Free-cash-flow guidance was trimmed to $160-210 million from $170-250 million, assuming $70-100 oil, because it now includes the $112 million upfront payment under the Ghana tax settlement agreed on 23 Nov. Capex guidance is unchanged at $200 million.

Bachem used its Zurich capital markets day to target average annual local-currency sales growth of 15-18% from a CHF 695 million 2025 base and a 33-35% EBITDA margin by 2031, with capex of 25-30% of sales in 2027-2031 and R&D spending quadrupling to about CHF 40 million. The shares fell as much as 12% (26 Nov).

Text Group, maker of LiveChat, reported fiscal second-quarter EBITDA of PLN 43.7 million and net profit of PLN 34 million, both up 19% and ahead of consensus, helped by cost control, and proposed a PLN 1.21 interim dividend. Recurring monthly revenue is still declining, but the shares rose about 17% to around PLN 43.

stories.headline: Berenberg Turns Buyer on Bayer With a €62 Target as Deutsche Bank Cuts Eutelsat to Sell; Arete Starts Anthropic at $300
stories.summary: Berenberg's Sebastian Bray raised Bayer to Buy from Hold on 26 Nov, keeping a €62 target, about 22% above the €50.68 close of 25 Nov, citing reduced glyphosate litigation risk after the US Supreme Court's Durnell ruling and a pharma unit without major patent expiries until after 2032. Deutsche Bank's Roshan Ranjit cut Eutelsat to Sell from Hold and slashed the target to €1.30 from €2.10, warning that renewing first-generation satellites before the IRIS constellation starts earning in 2032 will strain leverage; Eutelsat fell 3.4% (26 Nov). Bernstein lifted Genmab to Market Perform from Underperform. In New York, Arete initiated Anthropic at Buy with a $300 target on 25 Nov, against a $81.91 close the day before.
stories.market: The Bayer call leans on rotation from tech into healthcare; the Eutelsat downgrade left it the worst performer in France's SBF 120 on 26 Nov, while Deutsche Bank kept SES at Buy.

body: Berenberg's upgrade of Bayer rests on two pillars: litigation and pharma. The Durnell win at the US Supreme Court and a favourable Aretino outcome narrow the scope for further glyphosate claims, and the pharma division has repeatedly beaten expectations with its main patent cliffs pushed past 2032. The broker raised its 2027 and 2028 EPS estimates by 1.3% and 1.6% and noted Bayer's low correlation with US tech, after an 11% slide since the court approved its glyphosate settlement.

Deutsche Bank welcomed European backing for a sovereign satellite network but said Eutelsat's funding needs worry it: Europe would cover about 75% of IRIS financing, without firm commitments yet, and Eutelsat must first pay for renewing its first-generation fleet. The target cut to €1.30 from €2.10 followed two days of 3.4% declines in the shares (25-26 Nov).

Bernstein's Justin Smith upgraded Genmab to Market Perform, citing better R&D execution and the integration of two oncology drugs bought for $10 billion, and raised his 2026-2031 adjusted EPS growth estimate to 33% from 7%; he stayed neutral because of valuation and a wait for key pipeline data in 2028.

Arete's $300 Anthropic target, set on 25 Nov, is about 3.7 times the $81.91 close on 24 Nov, when the stock first dipped below its $83 IPO price. Other recent initiations ranged from Canaccord's $135 (Buy) and Oppenheimer's $150 to William Blair's $130 (Buy), with Seaport at Hold.

stories.headline: Foreign Investors Buy Indian Stocks for an 18th Straight Session, Taking November Inflows Past $15 Billion
stories.summary: Foreign institutional investors bought a net Rs 5,843 crore of Indian equities on 26 Nov, extending their buying streak to 18 sessions, and Reuters data put foreign portfolio inflows for November at about $15.16 billion through Thursday, a monthly record. On 25 Nov FIIs bought Rs 4,479.08 crore and domestic institutions Rs 4,018.72 crore, a combined Rs 8,497.80 crore that was the month's largest. JPMorgan said on 27 Nov that foreign long-only funds merely returning to benchmark weight could bring about $100 billion into India, setting a 29,000 end-2027 Nifty target and a 31,000 bull case.
stories.market: The flows help explain why big promoter blocks and the Mahanadi IPO were absorbed this week and why the rupee hit an eight-month high; JPMorgan favours financials, industrials, healthcare and consumer discretionary and is underweight IT and materials.

body: Foreign buying of Indian shares shows no sign of slowing. Provisional exchange data showed FIIs net bought Rs 5,843 crore in the cash market on 26 Nov, their 18th consecutive session of purchases. Reuters figures cited in coverage put November foreign portfolio inflows at about $15.16 billion through 26 Nov, surpassing the roughly $14.3 billion recorded through 25 Nov.
Domestic institutions also turned buyers on 25 Nov, only their second net-buying session of the month, purchasing Rs 4,018.72 crore alongside Rs 4,479.08 crore from foreign investors.

JPMorgan's strategists argued India could act as a diversification option away from crowded AI-heavy markets, forecasting MSCI India earnings growth of 12% in 2026 and 14% in 2027. Their base case is a Nifty of 29,000 by end-2027 with a 31,000 bull case, while flagging valuations and policy risks and recommending a selective approach that favours domestic cyclicals over exporters.

stories.headline: Ibovespa Soars 6.07% to 176,800, Its Best Day Since the First Election Round, on Soft Inflation and Talk of Trabuco at Finance
stories.summary: The Ibovespa jumped 6.07% to 176,799.84 on 26 Nov, its biggest one-day gain since 5 Oct, after mid-November IPCA-15 inflation came in at 0.22% against a median forecast of about 0.36% and reports that Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi could become finance minister. The commercial dollar fell 1.25% to R$5.744, a fourth straight decline; no appointment had been confirmed by the close.
stories.market: Financials (+8.98% sector index) led as Bradesco, Itaú and BTG Pactual rallied on the Trabuco speculation, while lower DI futures lifted rate-sensitive names such as Localiza and MRV.

body: Brazilian stocks staged their sharpest rally in seven weeks on 26 Nov. The Ibovespa closed at 176,799.84 after touching 177,024.45 in the final minutes, taking its two-session gain to 7.75% and more than reversing the 3.37% lost over the previous four sessions.

Two domestic catalysts drove the move. Mid-November IPCA-15 consumer prices rose 0.22% on the month, well below a median forecast of about 0.35-0.36%, pulling futures interest rates lower. At the same time, reports that Bradesco board chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi was in line to become finance minister in President Lula's next term, and that he had travelled to Brasília to meet the president, were read by investors as a signal of fiscal discipline. No appointment had been confirmed.

Financials did most of the lifting, with the sector index up 8.98%. Rate-sensitive groups also surged: the consumer index gained 7.40%, the real-estate index 7.71% and small caps 6.80%. Petrobras and Vale were helped by firmer oil and iron ore, though local reports stressed the day was driven by domestic factors.

Trading volume was a relatively modest R$25 billion, thinned by the US Thanksgiving holiday, with activity picking up into the close. The real strengthened 1.25% to R$5.744 per dollar, its fourth straight daily gain.

stories.headline: AEX Climbs 1.9% to 1,083 as Chipmakers, Adyen and Exor Rally and Pharming Rebounds 6%
stories.summary: Amsterdam's AEX rose 1.9% to 1,083.26 on 26 Nov in a broad advance, recovering from the three-month low hit the day before, as ASML and ASMI each gained about 3% and Adyen, CVC and Exor rose about 4%. Pharming bounced 6.2% after a 16.5% slide on Ruconest production problems, while Citi and UBS cut their Prosus targets to €45 and €63 even as the stock rose 2.6% to €30.04. Rabobank read the ECB minutes released the same day as a clear hint of a December rate increase.
stories.market: Chip-equipment makers led the recovery; Air France-KLM was the only decliner in the midcap index and EUR/USD stood near 1.0975 at the close (26 Nov).

body: The AEX closed 1.9% higher at 1,083.26 on 26 Nov, with nearly every Dutch share advancing in a quiet session while US markets were closed.
Semiconductor names led: ASML and ASM International gained about 3% each. Adyen, CVC and Exor topped the main index with rises of roughly 4%, and defence group Theon jumped 10% among midcaps.

Pharming recovered 6.2% after Jefferies called the previous day's 16.5% fall overdone; Prosus rose 2.6% despite target cuts from Citi (to €45 from €51) and UBS (to €63 from €69), both of which kept buy ratings.

Rabobank's Bas van Geffen said the ECB's meeting minutes clearly pointed to a December hike and that a pause afterwards is the most likely path. Separately, Pablo Hernández de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president in February, pending formal approval by EU leaders, after beating former DNB governor Klaas Knot.

stories.headline: IMF Tells the RBA to Keep a Tightening Bias as Inflation Runs Near 4%, While Miners Lift the ASX 200 0.8%
stories.summary: The IMF, concluding its 2026 Article IV review, said the Reserve Bank of Australia should keep a tightening bias until inflation is firmly heading back to its 2-3% target, projecting headline CPI of 4.0% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027 and growth slowing to 1.6% in 2027 from 1.9%. The S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.8% to 8,763.80 on 26 Nov as materials jumped 3.9% and energy 3.1%, the same day data showed business investment up 12.2% in the September quarter. The index added about 0.7% early on 27 Nov.
stories.market: The Australian dollar rose about 0.35% to around 66.6 US cents on 27 Nov after ending 26 Nov at 66.42 cents; gold and rare-earth miners such as Lynas (+7.9%) led Thursday's gains, while LendLease fell 9.8%.

body: The IMF's Article IV assessment backed the RBA's current stance, saying policy should stay agile and data-dependent with a tightening bias until inflation is clearly on track to the target, which it expects to be reached in the second half of 2027. It flagged upside risks from Middle East energy prices and wage pass-through.
The Fund sees unemployment rising to 4.9% from 4.5% and private business investment growth slowing sharply to 1.8% in 2027 from 7.8%.

On the ASX, Thursday's 0.8% gain to 8,763.80 was led by materials (+3.9%) and energy (+3.1%), with Ora Banda (+10.7%), Catalyst Metals (+9.7%) and Lynas (+7.9%) among the top movers; consumer staples fell 1.4%. The ABS reported a 12.2% jump in private capital expenditure in the September quarter, the most since 2011, driven by data centres.
Economists remain split on timing: UBS expects cuts only from August 2027, while Capital Economics said capacity pressures from AI-driven investment will keep the RBA on hold for now.

stories.headline: VN-Index Plunges 3.4% to 1,629.68 as a Proposed 35% US Tariff and Tech Selling Hit FPT and Vingroup Shares
stories.summary: Vietnam's VN-Index fell 57.77 points, or 3.42%, to 1,629.68 on 26 Nov, with 285 decliners against 46 gainers on the Ho Chi Minh City exchange and turnover above VND15.77 trillion (about $597 million). VIC dropped 6.28% and IT group FPT fell to its lowest since early 2023 at VND44,500. Investors cited Washington's proposed additional tariff of up to 35% on Vietnamese goods under a Section 301 probe, Fed hike fears and the global tech sell-off.
stories.market: The large-cap VN30 lost 49.7 points to 1,728.88; the tariff could fall to 20% under a reciprocal trade deal, with USTR hearings due from 25 Jan 2027 and a decision by 11 Mar 2027.

body: Selling swept Vietnam's main board on 26 Nov: the VN-Index shed 57.77 points to 1,629.68 and the VN30 lost 49.7 points to 1,728.88, with decliners outnumbering advancers more than six to one.

The trigger was the US proposal, under a Section 301 investigation, of an additional tariff of up to 35% on Vietnamese imports, the highest among the 14 economies named. It is not yet in force and could be cut to 20% under a reciprocal trade agreement.

Tech exposure added to the pressure. FPT fell VND1,550 to VND44,500 amid concern about AI displacing IT-services work, foreign net selling of about $600 million of its shares this year and possible removal from the VN-Diamond index. Jeweller PNJ also slid on a diamond-certification and buyback crisis.
